name: Scaling limiter, degree 3, extrema over the 3 Gauss-Lobatto points (2.11)
source: Zhang and Shu, J. Comput. Phys. 229 (2010), (2.8)-(2.11), Lemma 2.4, Theorem 2.5

claims.why: avg(p~) = ubar + theta (avg(p) - ubar) = ubar for any scalar theta
as on the cell, at the points where M_x and m_x are taken
between the Gauss-Lobatto points a quadratic can exceed them: p = -(y - y0)^2 with y0 not a point, [m, M] = [min, max] over the points, gives theta = 1 and p(y0) = 0 > M
the average is a positive combination of the point values (exact for degree <= 3), so M_x(points) >= ubar; theta(points) >= theta(cell) and the cell bound applies (the source, p. 10)
